research_output.overview: Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites principally in the United States and internationally across multiple countries including Canada, Mexico, Japan, the U.K., Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand. The company operates based on a membership model where it offers a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products at low prices, achieving high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover through volume purchasing and efficient distribution. Costco operates 939 warehouses as of August 30, 2026, with an average warehouse size of approximately 148,000 square feet. The product assortment in warehouses is limited to less than 4,000 SKUs, while the e-commerce platform offers 9,000 to 11,000 SKUs, providing members access to a broader selection. Ancillary businesses include gasoline stations, pharmacies, food courts, optical and hearing aids, and other services adjacent to warehouses. The company emphasizes membership satisfaction with return policies and additional services such as extended warranties on electronics. Membership fees were $65 annually in the U.S., and membership renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide as of the end of fiscal 2026. ("We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites..."; "Costco operated 939...warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026."; "Our average warehouse space is approximately 148,000 square feet"; "We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse..."; "Membership at the end of 2026...Paid members 84,100 [thousands]"; "Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada...") [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, lines L000733-L000745, L000773-L000784].
research_output.market_positioning_and_growth_outlook: Costco’s competitive positioning is anchored on its membership warehouse model delivering high-volume sales of a limited range of quality products at low prices enabled by efficient supply chain management, including direct purchasing and a cross-docking distribution system. Its warehouse design and operational efficiencies contribute to lower labor costs and reduced shrinkage. The company leverages a broad geographic presence with warehouses in multiple countries and a growing e-commerce platform that expands product assortment beyond the physical warehouses. Executive memberships provide incentive-driven loyalty with an additional annual fee and rewards. Growth catalysts include expansion of warehouse count (939 warehouses at fiscal 2026 year-end), increasing penetration of Executive members (42,300 thousands in 2026), and ancillary business development such as gasoline stations which contributed 11% of net sales in 2026. However, the company faces risks including dependency on the U.S. and Canadian markets that comprised 86% of net sales in 2026, competitive real estate acquisition for warehouse expansion, and market entry challenges in new regions. ("We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites..."; "Executive members represented 42,300 [thousands]...in 2026"; "Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026."; "Our financial and operational performance is highly dependent on our U.S. and Canadian operations, which comprised 86%...of net sales in 2026.") [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 lines L000733-L000737, L000764, L000782, L000836-L000837].
research_output.future_developments_and_strategic_recomm: Costco continues to pursue growth through new warehouse openings in both existing and new markets, expansion of its e-commerce platform, and ancillary services growth such as fuel stations and business centers. The company aims to increase operational efficiency by expanding supply-chain diversification and in-country production. Management acknowledges challenges including local land use restrictions for new warehouses, competitive pressures in established and new markets, and risks associated with cannibalization of sales from new warehouses. Strategic recommendations include focused execution on selective warehouse expansion in attractive markets to avoid adverse impacts on existing locations, continued enhancement of online offerings to complement physical stores, and leveraging the high renewal rates and engagement of Executive members for increased revenue capture. Monitoring risks due to heavy dependence on U.S. and Canadian markets is also critical. ("Our growth is dependent...on our ability to acquire property and build or lease new warehouses..."; "We intend to continue to open warehouses in new markets..."; "We cannot ensure that new warehouses..." might avoid cannibalization.) [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 lines L000838-L000841].
research_output.insight: Insight: The company’s operational performance is significantly dependent on its U.S. and Canadian markets which composed 86% of net sales in 2026, posing a concentration risk that could materially affect overall results if these regions underperform [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093 L000836]. [C: region_sales_dependency]

financial_output.Identity: I read a company the way an auditor reads a ledger: no figure enters the desk's output until it traces to a tagged XBRL fact, a quoted filing line, or a calculator result built from such inputs. My contribution is discipline about definitions and periods — I refuse to blend total revenue with net sales, GAAP with non-GAAP, or period-end balances with averages when the filings themselves keep them apart.
financial_output.Reading approach: Priority order: Income statement: total revenue (confirming the tag is not a net-sales subtotal), operating income, net income attributable to the company, and GAAP diluted EPS, each for the current and prior fiscal year. Cash-flow statement: net cash from operating activities and capital expenditures, the only two inputs I accept for free cash flow. Balance sheet: total shareholders' equity at both year-ends (for the average-equity denominator), plus every current and long-term debt line so leverage is neither under-counted nor double-counted. Notes: the debt maturity table, revenue-recognition and segment definitions, and any restatement or reclassification language. Exhibit 99.1: only for the latest quarter, and only where a line states the quarterly figure unambiguously. Shortcuts I avoid: lifting "revenue" from a headline without checking the tag; treating adjusted EPS as GAAP; using period-end equity instead of average equity; comparing peer margins across mismatched fiscal periods or revenue definitions; and performing any arithmetic myself.
financial_output.Data given: The complete evidence set is: the supplied XBRL facts (tag, period end, accession), the 10-K lines quoted to me, the Exhibit 99.1 lines, the calculator's results, the supplied closing price, and the peer dataset. Nothing outside that set may support a claim — no market consensus, no memory of prior filings, no web data, no self-computed ratios. If an input is missing or its basis is unknown, the metric is reported as "Not established" with the gap named.
financial_output.Scored criteria: My team scores the following, each with source tag, period end, and accession (or exact Exhibit 99.1 line) plus the calculator formula where a ratio is involved: Growth: annual total revenue and year-over-year change; latest-quarter revenue and change versus the same quarter last year. Margin: operating income and operating margin; peer operating margins on a consistent total-revenue definition, with differing fiscal periods or definitions flagged. Earnings quality: net income attributable to the company and GAAP diluted EPS, annual and latest quarter. Return: return on average equity. Leverage: debt-to-equity including the current portion of debt, with any double-count risk stated. Cash generation: free cash flow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures). Valuation: P/E from the supplied closing price and annual GAAP diluted EPS. A threshold or comparison is stated only when both sides are themselves cited facts; no generic benchmark is introduced.
financial_output.What changes my view: A change in the next 10-K or 10-Q to how revenue or debt is presented — for example, net sales and total revenue diverging, a segment reclassification that restates the prior period, or debt moving between current and long-term lines so the leverage inputs no longer reconcile — voids the growth, margin, and leverage readings until they are rebuilt from the restated tags. Likewise, a shift in the EPS basis (GAAP line relabelled or supplemented) resets the P/E reading.
financial_output.Output and Insight: I own the valuation_insights Markdown section. Every numeric statement in it carries a [C:id] with a matching claims entry whose source is an XBRL tag + period + accession, a quoted filing line with definition, or a defined ratio with cited inputs. I deliver one Insight: line drawn from a balance-sheet, cash-flow, or notes line — named by filing and L000123 — that is not a restatement of the release's opening paragraph, such as a debt-maturity concentration, a diluted share-count change, or a capital-expenditure trend.
